highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [![Engineering.com logo](https://www.engineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/engineering-com-logo-1.svg)](https://www.engineering.com) [Subscribe](https://www.engineering.com/subscribe/) [Industry News](https://www.engineering.com/category/industry/industry-news/) # Equinix expands NVIDIA collaboration for AI inference The new platform combines NVIDIA infrastructure and Together AI’s open-model platform across Equinix data centers. [Equinix, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=1428223178&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.equinix.com%2F&a=Equinix%2C+Inc.) announced a significant expansion of its longtime collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI. ![](https://www.engineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live-1.jpg) Equinix® Inference Exchange – Bringing inference closer to where data, users and applications live. As AI scales across models, providers and geographies, where inference runs is a strategic imperative that determines performance, cost and governance. Equinix Inference Exchange will give enterprises a faster path from AI experimentation to production, with secure, low-latency connectivity to the data, users and ecosystem they depend on. This collaboration brings together [NVIDIA’s validated Enterprise Reference Architecture](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=3290295942&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nvidia.com%2Fen-us%2Ftechnologies%2Fenterprise-reference-architecture%2F&a=NVIDIA%27s+validated+Enterprise+Reference+Architecture)s with Together AI’s inference platform, supporting more than 200 open-source models. Delivered through Equinix’s global data centers, it will provide connectivity to clouds, networks and AI providers through Equinix Fabric. The solution will be announced today at Equinix Horizon, the company’s inaugural customer and partner event, alongside [Equinix Fabric One](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=75577153&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsroom.equinix.com%2F2026-09-02-Equinix-Unveils-Equinix-Fabric-One%2C-Redefining-How-Enterprises-Connect-Across-AI%2C-Cloud-and-Networking-Infrastructure&a=Equinix%C2%AE%C2%A0Fabric+One%E2%84%A2), which will make it easier for enterprises to connect across globally distributed AI environments. ### **Where inference runs matters** The pace of enterprise AI adoption is outrunning the infrastructure needed to support it. As enterprise AI moves from experimentation to production, inference increasingly needs to run closer to the users, data and applications it serves across clouds, models, providers and geographies. This shift requires enterprises to determine not only how to deploy AI infrastructure, but where it should run and how it connects to the data, applications and workloads it depends on. Managing these distributed inference deployments introduces significant operational complexity at precisely the moment enterprises need greater control and visibility. Equinix brings unmatched scale and ecosystem density to this challenge, with more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps and over 10,500 businesses interconnected on its neutral exchange. Eight of the top 10 AI model providers and nine of the top 10 AI clouds are deployed with Equinix, underscoring the company’s position at the center of the AI ecosystem. ### **Built for choice and flexibility** Together AI is the latest addition to Equinix’s expansive AI ecosystem, bringing open-model flexibility and choice to enterprises deploying AI at scale. Revenue reached US$13.9 million, up 38.8% quarter-over-quarter, with gross margin expanding to 79.5%. Operating income and Adjusted EBITDA both turned positive. These results are the first evidence of the strategic direction we are taking. Two days ago in Hong Kong, we introduced the new AMBR: a company that builds specialized AI agents. This is a deliberate pivot. We were a digital wealth management business; we are becoming a technology company. We are doing so from a position of strength, not as a reaction. As of this week, we have two agents in the market. Ambre is our consumer agent for personal finance. It delivers the portfolio analysis, signals, monitoring and alerts that relationship managers have long provided to high-net-worth clients, but makes them available more broadly. It works across users' existing exchange and brokerage accounts and does not place orders — when a user decides to act, they are connected to our expert team. Ambre is currently available by invitation, starting with Amber Premium's verified client base. MIA is our marketing agent and the proof that this model produces revenue. Built and scaled inside our wholly-owned marketing businesses, MIA already runs a substantial share of day-to-day campaign operations for more than a hundred enterprise customers. It is now also available as a direct product. Ambre and MIA are the first two agents, not the full portfolio. Additional agents and the financial framework for the transition will be presented at our Investor Day, which we now expect to hold before year-end. highlights.content: # * [Home](/en/) * [News](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/) * [The Cloud & Hybrid Channel](/en/the-cloud-and-hybrid-channel/) # Equinix, Together AI, Nvidia partner on Inference Exchange Aims to give enterprises access to secure, low-latency AI inferencing By : [Georgia Butler](/en/profile/georgia-butler/) [Have your say](#comments) [![Preferred source](/static/img/google_preferred_source.172e670ec003.png)](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenterdynamics.com) Data center operator Equinix is working with Nvidia and Together AI on an Inferencing solution. Described as a distributed AI inference platform, the Inference Exchange uses Nvidia's Enterprise Reference Architecture and infrastructure and Together AI's inference platform, and is delivered through Equinix's global data centers. ![Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-.width-358.jpg) – Equinix Equinix has a footprint of more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps, and more than 10,500 businesses interconnected on its exchange. Via Equinix Fabric, the Inference Exchange will connect to clouds, networks, and AI providers. "AI is transforming enterprise technology at extraordinary speed, and the infrastructure decisions enterprises make today will define their competitive position for years to come. Equinix is uniquely positioned to deliver what this moment demands based on our nearly three decades building the trusted exchange where the world's enterprises run, connect, and orchestrate their most critical workloads," said Adaire Fox-Martin, CEO and president, Equinix. "Our longtime relationship with Nvidia delivers the accelerated computing foundation at the heart of modern AI, while Together AI's commitment to open ecosystems gives enterprises the flexibility to scale on their terms. Equinix Inference Exchange will enable architectures that are neutral by design, open by default, and engineered for exceptional performance." "Together AI was built on the conviction that open, accessible AI is what will define the industry moving forward, because enterprises shouldn't have to choose between model performance and operational flexibility," added Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO of Together AI. "What we are building with Equinix and Nvidia proves that model choice and performance are not trade-offs. They are the foundation of enterprise AI done right." Among the use cases the offering is targeting are metro Edge inference for organizations that require low latency for AI workloads, open model migration for enterprises looking to move from closed proprietary models to open-source alternatives using Together AI's platform, and sovereign AI workloads that need to run in specific locations. The Inference Exchange will be available from Q1 2027. AI cloud company [Together AI](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/together-ai-raises-800m-in-series-c-funding-round/) raised $800m in a Series C funding round in July 2026. The company is a known customer of [Rum Group](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/together-ai-taps-rumble-for-nvidia-blackwell-gpu-capacity/) and is planning to deploy hardware at an [L&T](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/lts-data-center-unit-to-host-nvidia-hardware-for-together-ai/) data center, while [Hypertec and 5C](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/hypertec-and-5c-target-europe-plan-2gw-roll-out-for-together-ai/) are aiming to roll out 2GW of capacity for the company. ## More in Cloud & Hyperscale * ![Network the cloud](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/Network_the_cloud.height-150.jpg) # [Network the cloud](/en/whitepapers/network-the-cloud-nokia/) * ![Natural Gas Power Plant](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/GettyImages-856558990.2e16d0ba.fill-280x185.jpg) # [Amazon acquires 8,000-acre site in Pecos, T...

As competitive advantages, the company cited its technological prowess as the inventor of flash memory and the production efficiency of its Yokkaichi and Kitakami plants. ##### Key Elements ![Kioxia Charts Path to AI Inference Era, Tapping Storage Demand Through Close Collaboration with NVIDIA](https://img.biggo.com/sRIkwKRGSJGXbPwTB50F8ce9tm1IoFU4WwVKsiA1xsA/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ2ZGQ2YzQ3LTZjNmUtNDg0MC05ZjljLTc4YjRlMjRlOTcxNV8xNzg4NDc4MzIzX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Kioxia Holdings, a major semiconductor memory manufacturer, held a media briefing on next-generation AI infrastructure in Tokyo on September 3, detailing its strategy for addressing the structural changes that generative AI adoption is bringing to the data center market. Makoto Hamada, General Manager of the SSD Business Division's Technology Planning Department, said, "The wave of infrastructure buildout driven by generative AI is unfolding right now, and this change is a once-in-a-lifetime transformation." He outlined a strategy to reposition flash memory and SSDs from mere data storage devices to core devices that power AI inference. According to research from U.S.-based McKinsey, global data center investment is projected to reach approximately $7 trillion (about ¥1,092.8 trillion) by 2030. Kioxia aims to deploy its products in this massive market as "main memory expansion" solutions and "devices that accelerate AI inference." ### CXL Memory Modules Targeting DRAM Replacement One of the key pillars of the company's strategy is its "CXL memory module," which combines proprietary XL-FLASH with a dedicated controller. With DRAM supply constrained in AI servers, Kioxia is proposing an approach that replaces a portion of DRAM with CXL memory modules to expand capacity. According to the company's estimates, compared to configuring main memory with DRAM alone, this approach can double memory capacity and boost performance by 1.3x at equivalent cost. At the briefing, Hamada noted that the rapid proliferation of generative AI "brings new demands and challenges to flash memory and SSDs, while simultaneously creating new business opportunities." He expressed the view that data centers will transform into "token factories" that generate massive volumes of tokens, and revealed plans to introduce SSDs that improve GPU utilization efficiency. ### Collaboration with NVIDIA and Competitive Advantages During the Q&A session, questions arose regarding the company's response to "Context Memory Storage" (CMX), a new storage tier for AI inference proposed by U.S.-based NVIDIA. Hamada acknowledged that competitor entry is naturally expected given the enormous market size, but expressed confidence, stating, "We work closely with NVIDIA and have opportunities to engage with their key players. We don't feel we're falling behind." Built on FastAPI, the gateway supports per-user key issuance, usage auditing, multi-model routing, and local model integration, with deployment requiring just a single Docker command or running a Python script on bare metal. The project explicitly excludes billing, content moderation, and high-availability clustering, positioning itself as a self-hosted control point for small and mid-sized teams. Meanwhile, Ollama recently launched a local proxy for Claude Desktop, allowing open models to run within Anthropic's application interface with support for slot remapping—underscoring the intensifying battle for control at the model access layer. ##### Key Elements ![New approach to enterprise LLM governance: unified intranet gateway control to eliminate exposed API keys and data leakage](https://img.biggo.com/CRK3Tm_4W6Y3vdy135j92NKdjsGpaK9OccQfkP3TEcY/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ4ODM1YzVjLWMyOTktNGYyYy04ZDQ5LWI1Njg5ZTkwN2I2Yl8xNzg4NDM1MTQ2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Enterprise adoption of large language models is shifting from "can we use it" to "how do we manage it properly." When employees paste API keys into work group chats and copy contracts and source code into public web-based chat interfaces, companies face not just an efficiency problem but a governance and security risk. llm-proxy-tk, a lightweight open-source gateway built on FastAPI, is attempting to turn LLMs into a corporate "tap water" system through an "intranet master valve" approach—unified access, per-person key issuance, visible usage, and the ability to cut off supply at any time. The project's core logic is straightforward: deploy an API gateway layer on the corporate intranet, route all employee and application model calls through this single entry point, and connect to any upstream provider behind it—DeepSeek, Claude, local Ollama, vLLM, or others. Employees receive an independent key issued by the gateway rather than the vendor's original API key. The gateway handles authentication, routing, metering, and auditing, while switching models underneath remains completely transparent to the caller. This approach directly targets three widespread pain points for small and mid-sized enterprises using LLMs. First is chaotic key management: one employee registers an account, shares the API key in a group chat, the entire team uses it collectively, and when limits are exceeded no one can explain why, and when keys leak no one can trace the source. Second is the risk of data leaving the corporate perimeter: employees, for convenience, paste product code, customer contracts, and even financial data directly into public web-based chat tools, making data flows completely uncontrollable. Third is model vendor lock-in: teams write code with Claude, generate Chinese content with DeepSeek, and run local deployments with Ollama—each client has its own endpoint and configuration, switching models requires modifying every integration point, and unified usage statistics are impossible to obtain. llm-proxy-tk attempts to solve these problems with a thin layer. This collaboration brings together [NVIDIA’s validated Enterprise Reference Architecture](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/technologies/enterprise-reference-architecture/) s with Together AI’s inference platform, supporting more than 200 open-source models. Delivered through Equinix’s global data centres, it will provide connectivity to clouds, networks and AI providers through Equinix Fabric. “AI is transforming enterprise technology at extraordinary speed, and the infrastructure decisions enterprises make today will define their competitive position for years to come. A second programme, Engineering Agentic AI Systems, will provide more technical training in designing, building, and deploying agentic systems. Topics will include agent architecture, tool integration, orchestration, memory, deployment, and the use of no-code, low-code, and code-based frameworks. ## Why does it matter? Agentic AI could change work more substantially than tools that mainly generate text or images because it can plan and execute multi-step tasks. India is beginning to [build training](https://dig.watch/updates/indian-government-proposes-ai-training-for-10-million-youth) around that shift, giving learners practical experience in automating workflows, building AI agents, and working with systems that can perform parts of complex jobs under human oversight. ***Would you like to learn more about AI, tech, and digital diplomacy? Revenue reached US$13.9 million, up 38.8% quarter-over-quarter, with gross margin expanding to 79.5%. Operating income and Adjusted EBITDA both turned positive. These results are the first evidence of the strategic direction we are taking. Two days ago in Hong Kong, we introduced the new AMBR: a company that builds specialized AI agents. This is a deliberate pivot. We were a digital wealth management business; we are becoming a technology company. We are doing so from a position of strength, not as a reaction. As of this week, we have two agents in the market. Ambre is our consumer agent for personal finance. It delivers the portfolio analysis, signals, monitoring and alerts that relationship managers have long provided to high-net-worth clients, but makes them available more broadly. It works across users' existing exchange and brokerage accounts and does not place orders — when a user decides to act, they are connected to our expert team. Ambre is currently available by invitation, starting with Amber Premium's verified client base. MIA is our marketing agent and the proof that this model produces revenue. Built and scaled inside our wholly-owned marketing businesses, MIA already runs a substantial share of day-to-day campaign operations for more than a hundred enterprise customers. It is now also available as a direct product. Ambre and MIA are the first two agents, not the full portfolio. Additional agents and the financial framework for the transition will be presented at our Investor Day, which we now expect to hold before year-end. Until then, our priority is disciplined execution on what we have just launched." Vicky Wang, President of Amber International, said: "Earlier this week, on September 1, we officially unveiled the new AMBR, focused on building specialized AI agents for high-value, high-stakes use cases. AI Agents.content: # Exclusive: New bill cracks down on AI agents after Hugging Face breach ![](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.axios.com%2FcsbomMKRj0kPnUXAWXrApyCaAI0%3D%2F52x0%2Fsmart%2F2024%2F02%2F14%2F1707954926919.jpg&w=128&q=75) Add Axios as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. ![Illustration of a tiny robot breaking out a chat box. ](https://images.axios.com/J0nylSYocA8hI5frBeeI6VnTe2E=/1920x1080/smart/2024/10/23/204346-1729716226915.jpg?w=3840) Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios Reps. Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.) and Mike Lawler (R-N.Y.) are introducing a new bill today, first shared with Axios, aimed at securing AI agents amid a [growing number of safety incidents](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/28/hugging-face-openai-cybersecurity-defense) involving rogue agents. **Why it matters:** Washington has been slow to respond to the safety and security concerns raised by [OpenAI's Hugging Face hack](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/26/openai-hugging-face-technical-report-ai-hack) and other testing incidents involving agents that took unauthorized actions over the last two months. **Driving the news**: The Stop Rogue AI Act directs Commerce's National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop and publish standards, guidelines and best practices for how organizations can securely deploy AI agents. **Between the lines**: Gottheimer told Axios in a statement that the bill is designed to help companies identify agents running on their networks and "know exactly who's behind them." **The intrigue:** While the standards are voluntary for most organizations, the bill would push for federal contractors bidding for new deals to meet the NIST standards. **The big picture:** Gottheimer and Lawler's bill joins a growing number of legislative attempts on Capitol Hill to bring transparency and security to AI agents' actions. **What they're saying**: "Right now, AI agents are running loose in our networks, and nobody can see them or verify who built them — making it increasingly hard to stop them," Gottheimer told Axios. "That's a five-alarm security risk." **Reality check:** Washington has struggled to keep up with the security advancements — and subsequent concerns — of AI models and agents, and other AI bills haven't gained much traction in Congress this session. **Yes, but:** Gottheimer and Lawler's bill has the support of several U.S. companies and industry trade groups, including Palo Alto Networks, GoDaddy, Infoblox, the AI Policy Network, and Alliance for Secure AI. **Go deeper:** [AI's agent containment problem is getting harder](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/01/openai-hugging-face-ai-agent-security) ##### What to read next ![](data:image/webp;base64,...

AI Agents.content: # Sigenergy Ranks #1 Globally in S&P Global Energy H1 2026 Residential Energy Storage Market Tracker September 02, 2026 23:54 ET  | Source: [Sigenergy](/en/search/organization/Sigenergy%2520Technology%2520(Hong%2520Kong)%2520Limited) Sigenergy SHANGHAI, Sept. 02, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sigenergy has just secured the No. 1 global ranking by MWh shipments in S&P Global Energy’s Residential Energy Storage Market Tracker (H1 2026), capturing a leading **14% market share**. This top-tier global recognition validates the company's rapid worldwide expansion and user-led innovation across the residential energy storage sector. ![Sigenergy](https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/2837cdb1-aa8d-4dfc-9034-8034d853ca2b/no-1-poster.jpg) ![Sigenergy](https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/2837cdb1-aa8d-4dfc-9034-8034d853ca2b/no-1-poster.jpg) **Multi-Regional Growth and Global Market Footprint** Sigenergy’s global leadership is propelled by balanced growth across key international territories rather than a single region. Backed by strong traction in Europe, resilient momentum in Oceania, and rebounding markets in Africa, the company secured top market positions across multiple countries. To date, Sigenergy supports its worldwide customer base through a robust global network comprising over 170 distributors and 25,000+ registered installers spanning more than 120 countries. Amid an accelerating global energy transition, Sigenergy capitalized on surging demand for distributed energy by executing its visionary "AI in All" strategy. During the first half of 2026, this strategy propelled the introduction of four major product breakthroughs: the next-generation SigenStor Neo all-in-one ESS, SigenFlux heat pumps, Sigen EVAC 2 smart EV chargers, and SigenMate micro energy storage systems. Together, these innovations form a unified powerhouse capable of seamlessly generating, storing, optimizing, and protecting household energy. **AI Empowers Energy: Advancing the “AI in All” Global Strategy** In the first half, Sigenergy launched SigenAgent, the industry's first full-domain AI agent designed to redefine AI-powered energy management. Its AI agent squad—Energy Manager, System Doctor, Power Trader and Business Assistant—supports key applications across home energy, power station O&M, power trading and enterprise energy management, making complex energy tasks simpler and more efficient. Furthermore, the company globally rolled out **mySigen App 4.0** powered with SigenAgent, enhancing intelligent energy management capabilities through AI algorithms and energy data analytics. Continuous investment in R&D and technological accumulation further strengthens Sigenergy’s competitive foundation and supports sustainable long-term growth. **Smart Manufacturing Strengthens Global Delivery Capability** Following its Main Board listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in April 2026, Sigenergy significantly strengthened its supply chain infrastructure: **The Nantong Smart Energy Hub**, officially commissioned in March 2026, represents a major milestone in Sigenergy’s global intelligent manufacturing strategy. The facility supports annual production capacity exceeding 300,000 units of inverters and energy storage PACKs, integrating R&D, manufacturing and digital management capabilities. LLMs.content: Feature Story | 3-Sep-2026 # Who does AI consider an expert? New benchmark shows bias across 22 LLMs Complexity Science Hub [![Interactive Visualization ](https://mediasvc.eurekalert.org/Api/v1/Multimedia/d5b6e588-47b5-4a17-95e7-6a9fa8f23eeb/Rendition/low-res/Content/Public)](/multimedia/1149771) **image: In the interactive visualization “[Whose name comes up](https://vis.csh.ac.at/whosenamecomesup/)”, users can explore how often each physicist was recommended across runs and view individual chatbot performance per evaluation metric.** [view more](/multimedia/1149771) Credit: Complexity Science Hub (CSH) **Researchers at the Complexity Science Hub (CSH) benchmarked language models on their ability to recommend experts in academia. The models tend to favor white, male, senior and U.S.-based scholars, while improving factual accuracy can come at the expense of social representation. The findings are based on a trilogy of studies, and feed into the interactive visualization “Whose name comes up?”** **THE STUDY IN A NUTSHELL** * Researchers developed *LLMScholarBench*, a benchmark that uses nine metrics to evaluate the technical quality and social representation of LLM-generated expert recommendations. * Across three studies, they audited up to 43 LLMs. * In physics, LLMs systematically favor white male senior scholars from the US and make factual errors in around 20% of recommendations. * User interventions (such as targeted prompts) improve either technical quality or social representation, indicating a trade-off between the two. * **The interactive visualization [“Whose name comes up?”](https://vis.csh.ac.at/whosenamecomesup/)** lets users explore the results for each chatbot tested on a filterable line chart and a leaderboard. It brings together findings from three related papers, [one of which was presented at KDD 2026](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3770855.3817543) in August. AI chatbots powered by large language models (LLMs) are widely used as recommender systems. While accelerating access to information, AI can also give factually wrong responses or propagate societal biases. This matters in many contexts, including when AI is used to recommend expertise. Biased expert recommendations can deny important career opportunities for those who are left out. For example, in academia, explains computer scientist [Lisette Espín-Noboa](https://csh.ac.at/lisette-espin-noboa/), who is a CSH Research Fellow: “A conference organizer may use LLMs to find potential keynote speakers. If your name never comes up, you are invisible and will miss out.” Espín-Noboa and her colleagues wanted to better understand the quality of AI-generated expert recommendations. “We tested state-of-the-art LLMs, including open weight models like LLaMA and DeepSeek as well as proprietary models like Gemini and GPT,” she explains. **First**, the researchers looked for bias in how AI tools recommend experts in physics. “When we initially asked six LLMs to find scholars in specific physics subfields, they mostly cited real scientists but mismatched their field 40% of the time, on average. Moreover, the models tended to favor male senior experts from the US and those who are highly cited”, Espín-Noboa summarizes the main findings. **Next**, they introduced *LLMScholarBench*, a benchmark with nine metrics to assess technical quality and social representation, and tested four user interventions across 22 LLMs. The interventions improved either factual accuracy or social representation, but not both at the same time. **Finally**, they examined whether roles like “you are a student looking for a supervisor” or “a recruiter looking for a professor”, language, and geographic location affect recommendations across six academic disciplines. Geographic location influenced who was recommended, while language and role did not. --- ### **INTERACTIVE VISUALIZATION “WHOSE NAME COMES UP?”** Together with CSH [data visualization](https://csh.ac.at/visuals/) expert [Yi Zhe Ang](h...

LLMs.content: ![]() ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-light.svg) ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-dark.svg) # OpenAI Rival Moonshot Makes Blockbuster $50 Billion Move ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alibaba.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/microsoft.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/amazon.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alphabet.svg) Chinese artificial-intelligence startup Moonshot AI is preparing one of the biggest tests yet of investor appetite for China's AI boom, confidentially filing for a **Hong Kong IPO that could raise roughly $3 billion** while carrying a valuation of about **$50 billion**. A successful offering would give public investors a rare benchmark for valuing a standalone Chinese large-language-model developer as competition with U.S. AI leaders intensifies. Moonshot was founded in 2023 by AI researcher Yang Zhilin and develops the **Kimi** family of large language models. Its latest Kimi K3 model has **2.8 trillion parameters**, native multimodal capabilities and a one-million-token context window, targeting coding, knowledge work and complex reasoning. The Beijing-based company is working with **Goldman Sachs, China International Capital Corp. and Deutsche Bank** on the proposed offering, according to Reuters. The release, first detailed by [MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/09/02/perplexity-open-sources-lily-a-rust-metal-inference-engine-for-qwen3-6-35b-a3b-on-apple-silicon/), positions Lily as the local half of Hybrid Compute, the split-execution mode inside the Perplexity Computer Mac app that divides work between on-device processing and Perplexity’s cloud. The move matters beyond one product feature. It is a rare case of a well-funded AI company shipping a purpose-built, hand-optimized inference runtime instead of leaning on general-purpose frameworks like PyTorch or MLX, then giving the code away for free. For engineers who build local-first AI tools, and for the wider Apple Silicon inference ecosystem that already includes llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio, Lily’s arrival on September 2, 2026 raises a direct question: is narrow, single-model specialization now the fastest way to squeeze more tokens per second out of a MacBook, and does it threaten to fragment the local-inference toolchain that developers currently rely on. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. A Rust runtime loads the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B checkpoint and manages session state and the generation loop. That finding — Mythos 5.1 demonstrating 1.6 to 2.1 times higher performance than Claude Mythos Preview on LinuxArena stealth evaluations, with slightly increased chain-of-thought controllability — arrived in the same document that applied a CB-1 dangerous-capability designation to a generally available model for the first time in Anthropic's history. Enterprise artificial intelligence has a memory problem, and [Coworker.ai](http://coworker.ai) believes solving it could dramatically reduce the cost and complexity of deploying AI inside large organizations. The startup today launched OM2, an organizational memory layer that continuously transforms information from workplace applications into a structured, permission-aware representation of a business. According to Coworker.ai, using this precomputed context can reduce the token cost associated with enterprise information retrieval by ninefold while producing answers 64% faster than conventional tool-calling systems. When combined with the company’s model-routing technology, Coworker.ai says savings can reach as much as 51 times the cost of standard approaches. In company evaluations, OM2-generated answers were preferred on quality 84.5% of the time. Those are substantial claims in a market where enterprises are increasingly concerned about the cost, reliability and governance of generative AI. “Token costs are exploding, and most AI still doesn’t understand how to be effective inside a real company,” Coworker.ai cofounder and CEO [Alex Calder](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alextcalder/) said in announcing the product. **The hidden cost of reconstructing a company** Large language models generally do not maintain a durable understanding of an organization between sessions. A model answering a question about a customer, project or internal policy must first be supplied with the relevant context. Enterprise AI systems commonly obtain that information through retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG. In a typical implementation, the system searches documents, messages and databases when a question arrives, places potentially relevant material into a model’s context window and asks the model to compose an answer. That approach gives AI access to private or current information that was not included in its original training. It can also be inefficient. Every new question may trigger another search across the same collection of systems. The AI must repeatedly sift through documents, interpret overlapping passages and reconstruct relationships that the organization already established elsewhere. An account’s history, for example, might be distributed across Salesforce records, Slack conversations, meeting transcripts and project-management updates. Coworker.ai says more than half of some enterprise AI token budgets can be consumed by this process of retrieving and reconstructing context. Rather than treating that overhead as an unavoidable cost, OM2 attempts to move much of the work out of the query itself. As information enters the system, OM2 extracts discrete facts and connects them to relevant people, accounts, projects, decisions and events. Those facts are computed once, updated as the underlying business changes and reused across subsequent requests. The distinction is important. The pitch, first reported by TechCrunch, flips the usual AI safety conversation on its head and raises fresh questions about who gets to decide what a model is allowed to say. There's a quiet corner of the open-source AI world where researchers have spent the last couple of years figuring out how to surgically remove the part of a language model that says no. The technique, known as [abliteration](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/03/abliteration-ai-is-making-a-business-out-of-removing-ai-guardrails/), works by identifying the internal 'refusal direction' inside a model's neural activations and essentially deleting it, leaving behind a model that will answer just about anything you ask it. Now a startup called Abliteration.AI wants to turn that trick into a business, and it's doing so with a pitch that sounds almost counterintuitive: strip away the guardrails to make everyone safer. The company's argument, as laid out in a report from [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/03/abliteration-ai-is-making-a-business-out-of-removing-ai-guardrails/), goes like this. Cybercriminals already have access to jailbroken and abliterated versions of popular open-weight models, since the technique doesn't require much more than a laptop with a decent GPU and some publicly available code. Security researchers, red teamers and defenders, meanwhile, are often stuck working with heavily filtered commercial models that refuse to generate the kind of malicious phishing text, malware code or social engineering scripts they'd need to actually test whether a client's defenses hold up. Abliteration.AI's bet is that closing that gap by giving defenders the same unrestricted tools as attackers actually improves cybersecurity outcomes, rather than making things worse. It's not a completely novel idea. Penetration testers have long used adversarial tools that mimic real attacker behavior, and the broader security industry has always operated on some version of 'you have to think like a hacker to stop one.' What's new here is the packaging: turning what used to be a niche, DIY technique passed around in [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co) repos and machine learning forums into a polished, presumably paid, product aimed at enterprise security teams. That commercialization is exactly what makes AI safety researchers nervous. Advertisement The timing isn't an accident either. Over the past two years, the open-weight model ecosystem, anchored by releases from companies like Meta's Llama family and Mistral, has made it dramatically easier for anyone to download a capable model and modify it however they like, since the weights themselves are public. Once you have the weights, abliteration is a well-documented process, not a trade secret. That's part of why this business model exists at all. If the major labs kept their best models fully closed and API-gated the way OpenAI and Anthropic largely do, there'd be much less raw material for a company like Abliteration.AI to work with in the first place. HiddenLayer plans to put the capital towards expanding its enterprise platform, with a particular focus on its Agentic Runtime Security offering and a newly launched product called Agent Harness Security. The latter builds on the existing Runtime Security module, extending protection to AI coding agents while they operate, and is aimed at businesses bringing autonomous coding tools into their development environments. The Series B follows a year of rapid expansion for the company. Annual recurring revenue climbed more than tenfold, and HiddenLayer added over 50 new platform customers spanning securities brokerage, banking, insurance, accounting, government, technology, IT services, pharmaceuticals, airlines, and the US defence and intelligence sectors. Its international customer base grew too, taking in one of the world’s largest pharmaceutical firms alongside several premium automotive and food and beverage brands. Separately, the company also helps a major frontier model provider secure a platform used by more than 700 million people weekly. Much of this momentum stems from HiddenLayer’s research division, which holds 39 granted patents and a further 65 pending, covering areas such as adversarial detection, model protection and AI threat analysis. The team built the first Adversarial Prompt Engineering Taxonomy and continues to track emerging risks across generative, predictive and agentic AI, having identified numerous vulnerabilities throughout the AI stack, from foundation models through to supporting tools and infrastructure. HiddenLayer secures agentic, generative and predictive AI applications across the full AI lifecycle, covering everything from discovery and AI supply chain security to attack simulation and runtime protection. Open Source AI.content: [Pricing](/pricing) [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # New approach to enterprise LLM governance: unified intranet gateway control to eliminate exposed API keys and data leakage [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) The open-source project llm-proxy-tk proposes a lightweight intranet gateway to centrally govern enterprise large language model usage, addressing three major pain points: exposed API keys, data leaving the corporate perimeter, and vendor lock-in. Built on FastAPI, the gateway supports per-user key issuance, usage auditing, multi-model routing, and local model integration, with deployment requiring just a single Docker command or running a Python script on bare metal. The project explicitly excludes billing, content moderation, and high-availability clustering, positioning itself as a self-hosted control point for small and mid-sized teams. Meanwhile, Ollama recently launched a local proxy for Claude Desktop, allowing open models to run within Anthropic's application interface with support for slot remapping—underscoring the intensifying battle for control at the model access layer. ##### Key Elements ![New approach to enterprise LLM governance: unified intranet gateway control to eliminate exposed API keys and data leakage](https://img.biggo.com/CRK3Tm_4W6Y3vdy135j92NKdjsGpaK9OccQfkP3TEcY/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ4ODM1YzVjLWMyOTktNGYyYy04ZDQ5LWI1Njg5ZTkwN2I2Yl8xNzg4NDM1MTQ2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Enterprise adoption of large language models is shifting from "can we use it" to "how do we manage it properly." When employees paste API keys into work group chats and copy contracts and source code into public web-based chat interfaces, companies face not just an efficiency problem but a governance and security risk. llm-proxy-tk, a lightweight open-source gateway built on FastAPI, is attempting to turn LLMs into a corporate "tap water" system through an "intranet master valve" approach—unified access, per-person key issuance, visible usage, and the ability to cut off supply at any time. The project's core logic is straightforward: deploy an API gateway layer on the corporate intranet, route all employee and application model calls through this single entry point, and connect to any upstream provider behind it—DeepSeek, Claude, local Ollama, vLLM, or others. Employees receive an independent key issued by the gateway rather than the vendor's original API key. The gateway handles authentication, routing, metering, and auditing, while switching models underneath remains completely transparent to the caller. This approach directly targets three widespread pain points for small and mid-sized enterprises using LLMs. First is chaotic key management: one employee registers an account, shares the API key in a group chat, the entire team uses it collectively, and when limits are exceeded no one can explain why, and when keys leak no one can trace the source. Second is the risk of data leaving the corporate perimeter: employees, for convenience, paste product code, customer contracts, and even financial data directly into public web-based chat tools, making data flows completely uncontrollable. The new models are fully open—including model weights, code, training data and methodologies—allowing researchers and developers to inspect, reproduce and adapt the models for their own work. The six models share a core architecture, vocabulary, training methodology, interfaces and deployment tooling, with a smaller vocabulary for the 0.9B model. IFM's dynamic model routing technique directs tasks to the most cost-effective model and provides developers with a practical path from prototype to production. Plus, the fully open code, training data and recipes are a significant step forward in transparency, well beyond the "open weights" dialogue that has dominated AI industry headlines over recent weeks. Launched by [Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4766591-1&h=571811556&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmbzuai.ac.ae%2F&a=Mohamed+bin+Zayed+University+of+Artificial+Intelligence) (MBZUAI) in May 2025, IFM now employs AI researchers, scientists and developers across three offices in Silicon Valley, Paris and Abu Dhabi. Nvidia has agreed to acquire New York City-based AI company Hugging Face for a whopping $12,930,300,000. Hugging Face, which many describe as a sort of GitHub for AI models, is home to an expansive open-source library of AI tools. Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang [describes](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-to-acquire-hugging-face/) Hugging Face as “a vibrant home for the open model developer community.” “More than 18 million developers, researchers and creators use Hugging Face to share more than 3 million models, 500,000 datasets and 1 million applications. More than 200,000 companies use the platform to discover, evaluate, customize and deploy AI,” Huang continues. Despite spending nearly $13 billion to acquire Hugging Face, Huang says Nvidia will keep Hugging Face alive as an open platform. “Hugging Face will continue to support open source and open weight models from across the ecosystem, from every model builder. It will continue to support multi-cloud and multi-accelerator development and deployment, so builders can use the hardware and infrastructure that best fit their work,” Huang promises. Nvidia has demonstrated a longstanding commitment to open AI models and has been the largest contributor of open models and data to the Hugging Face community since early 2025. As of today, Nvidia has released more than 500 models and over 250 open datasets on Hugging Face. Many other familiar companies also release open data on Hugging Face, including Meta, Microsoft, and AMD, to name a few. Huang says open models enable startups, businesses, universities, and public institutions to build more powerful AI models without training every model entirely from scratch. “That is how AI can advance safely, strengthen cybersecurity and sovereignty, accelerate innovation, and reach factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms and Main Street businesses around the world,” Huang explains. Nvidia has benefited greatly from the proliferation of AI models and technology, which require the very chips Nvidia makes. In the past five years, propelled significantly by AI growth, Nvidia’s stock price has increased by nearly 900 percent. The company’s market cap has grown from around $300 billion to $5.5 trillion at the time of writing. Nvidia’s stock rose from just shy of $23 per share to nearly $228. The more accessible AI models are to users, the more in demand Nvidia’s chips become. “As the opportunity for open models accelerates, Hugging Face can serve the global AI community at unprecedented scale. Nvidia’s infrastructure, engineering and global reach can help improve platform reliability, safety, model evaluation, inference and deployment capabilities, while preserving the open ecosystem that made Hugging Face foundational,” Huang says. --- Image creditsNvidia Affiliate Disclosure PetaPixel articles may include affiliate links; we may earn a commission if you buy through one. The final deal amount is $12.93 billion. This is how much Nvidia has agreed to pay to acquire Hugging Face. Three years ago, Hugging Face was valued at a significantly lower amount, $4.5 billion. [Equinix, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=1428223178&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.equinix.com%2F&a=Equinix%2C+Inc.) announced a significant expansion of its longtime collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI. ![](https://www.engineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live-1.jpg) Equinix® Inference Exchange – Bringing inference closer to where data, users and applications live. As AI scales across models, providers and geographies, where inference runs is a strategic imperative that determines performance, cost and governance. Equinix Inference Exchange will give enterprises a faster path from AI experimentation to production, with secure, low-latency connectivity to the data, users and ecosystem they depend on. This collaboration brings together [NVIDIA’s validated Enterprise Reference Architecture](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=3290295942&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nvidia.com%2Fen-us%2Ftechnologies%2Fenterprise-reference-architecture%2F&a=NVIDIA%27s+validated+Enterprise+Reference+Architecture)s with Together AI’s inference platform, supporting more than 200 open-source models. Delivered through Equinix’s global data centers, it will provide connectivity to clouds, networks and AI providers through Equinix Fabric. The solution will be announced today at Equinix Horizon, the company’s inaugural customer and partner event, alongside [Equinix Fabric One](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=75577153&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsroom.equinix.com%2F2026-09-02-Equinix-Unveils-Equinix-Fabric-One%2C-Redefining-How-Enterprises-Connect-Across-AI%2C-Cloud-and-Networking-Infrastructure&a=Equinix%C2%AE%C2%A0Fabric+One%E2%84%A2), which will make it easier for enterprises to connect across globally distributed AI environments. ### **Where inference runs matters** The pace of enterprise AI adoption is outrunning the infrastructure needed to support it. As enterprise AI moves from experimentation to production, inference increasingly needs to run closer to the users, data and applications it serves across clouds, models, providers and geographies. This shift requires enterprises to determine not only how to deploy AI infrastructure, but where it should run and how it connects to the data, applications and workloads it depends on. Managing these distributed inference deployments introduces significant operational complexity at precisely the moment enterprises need greater control and visibility. Equinix brings unmatched scale and ecosystem density to this challenge, with more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps and over 10,500 businesses interconnected on its neutral exchange. Eight of the top 10 AI model providers and nine of the top 10 AI clouds are deployed with Equinix, underscoring the company’s position at the center of the AI ecosystem. ### **Built for choice and flexibility** Together AI is the latest addition to Equinix’s expansive AI ecosystem, bringing open-model flexibility and choice to enterprises deploying AI at scale. Described as a distributed AI inference platform, the Inference Exchange uses Nvidia's Enterprise Reference Architecture and infrastructure and Together AI's inference platform, and is delivered through Equinix's global data centers. ![Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-.width-358.jpg) – Equinix Equinix has a footprint of more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps, and more than 10,500 businesses interconnected on its exchange. Equinix is uniquely positioned to deliver what this moment demands based on our nearly three decades building the trusted exchange where the world's enterprises run, connect, and orchestrate their most critical workloads," said Adaire Fox-Martin, CEO and president, Equinix. "Our longtime relationship with Nvidia delivers the accelerated computing foundation at the heart of modern AI, while Together AI's commitment to open ecosystems gives enterprises the flexibility to scale on their terms. Equinix Inference Exchange will enable architectures that are neutral by design, open by default, and engineered for exceptional performance." "Together AI was built on the conviction that open, accessible AI is what will define the industry moving forward, because enterprises shouldn't have to choose between model performance and operational flexibility," added Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO of Together AI. "What we are building with Equinix and Nvidia proves that model choice and performance are not trade-offs. They are the foundation of enterprise AI done right." Among the use cases the offering is targeting are metro Edge inference for organizations that require low latency for AI workloads, open model migration for enterprises looking to move from closed proprietary models to open-source alternatives using Together AI's platform, and sovereign AI workloads that need to run in specific locations. Kioxia emphasized close collaboration with NVIDIA and outlined plans to make AI inference SSDs a core earnings driver. As competitive advantages, the company cited its technological prowess as the inventor of flash memory and the production efficiency of its Yokkaichi and Kitakami plants. ##### Key Elements ![Kioxia Charts Path to AI Inference Era, Tapping Storage Demand Through Close Collaboration with NVIDIA](https://img.biggo.com/sRIkwKRGSJGXbPwTB50F8ce9tm1IoFU4WwVKsiA1xsA/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ2ZGQ2YzQ3LTZjNmUtNDg0MC05ZjljLTc4YjRlMjRlOTcxNV8xNzg4NDc4MzIzX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Kioxia Holdings, a major semiconductor memory manufacturer, held a media briefing on next-generation AI infrastructure in Tokyo on September 3, detailing its strategy for addressing the structural changes that generative AI adoption is bringing to the data center market. Makoto Hamada, General Manager of the SSD Business Division's Technology Planning Department, said, "The wave of infrastructure buildout driven by generative AI is unfolding right now, and this change is a once-in-a-lifetime transformation." He outlined a strategy to reposition flash memory and SSDs from mere data storage devices to core devices that power AI inference. According to research from U.S.-based McKinsey, global data center investment is projected to reach approximately $7 trillion (about ¥1,092.8 trillion) by 2030. Kioxia aims to deploy its products in this massive market as "main memory expansion" solutions and "devices that accelerate AI inference." ### CXL Memory Modules Targeting DRAM Replacement One of the key pillars of the company's strategy is its "CXL memory module," which combines proprietary XL-FLASH with a dedicated controller. With DRAM supply constrained in AI servers, Kioxia is proposing an approach that replaces a portion of DRAM with CXL memory modules to expand capacity. According to the company's estimates, compared to configuring main memory with DRAM alone, this approach can double memory capacity and boost performance by 1.3x at equivalent cost. At the briefing, Hamada noted that the rapid proliferation of generative AI "brings new demands and challenges to flash memory and SSDs, while simultaneously creating new business opportunities." He expressed the view that data centers will transform into "token factories" that generate massive volumes of tokens, and revealed plans to introduce SSDs that improve GPU utilization efficiency. ### Collaboration with NVIDIA and Competitive Advantages During the Q&A session, questions arose regarding the company's response to "Context Memory Storage" (CMX), a new storage tier for AI inference proposed by U.S.-based NVIDIA. Hamada acknowledged that competitor entry is naturally expected given the enormous market size, but expressed confidence, stating, "We work closely with NVIDIA and have opportunities to engage with their key players. We don't feel we're falling behind." He also noted that Kioxia has daily opportunities to converse with NVIDIA's key players, and expressed interest in storage requirements that will be needed in AI-enabled PCs and physical AI in the future. Infra & Chips.content: ![ITWire](/brand/itwire-logo-template.ad986f71.png) # Equinix Accelerates AI Inference for Enterprises with NVIDIA and Together AI [Equinix](/tag/equinix/) | Published 4 Sept 2026 ![Adaire Fox-Martin, Chief Executive Officer and President at Equinix](https://media.itwire.com/2026/09/03/equinix-accelerates-ai-inference-for-enterprises-with-nvidia-and-together-ai-fbb0004d4893.jpg) **COMPANY NEWS:** Equinix Inference Exchange combines NVIDIA Enterprise Reference Architectures, Together AI’s inference platform and Equinix’s global infrastructure to optimise deployment speed, flexibility and cost efficiency Equinix, the world’s digital infrastructure company, has announced a significant expansion of its longtime collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI. As AI scales across models, providers and geographies, where inference runs is a strategic imperative that determines performance, cost and governance. Equinix Inference Exchange will give enterprises a faster path from AI experimentation to production, with secure, low-latency connectivity to the data, users and ecosystem they depend on. This collaboration brings together [NVIDIA’s validated Enterprise Reference Architecture](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/technologies/enterprise-reference-architecture/) s with Together AI’s inference platform, supporting more than 200 open-source models. Delivered through Equinix’s global data centres, it will provide connectivity to clouds, networks and AI providers through Equinix Fabric. “AI is transforming enterprise technology at extraordinary speed, and the infrastructure decisions enterprises make today will define their competitive position for years to come. Equinix is uniquely positioned to deliver what this moment demands based on our nearly three decades building the trusted exchange where the world’s enterprises run, connect and orchestrate their most critical workloads,” said Adaire Fox-Martin, Chief Executive Officer and President, Equinix. “Our longtime relationship with NVIDIA delivers the accelerated computing foundation at the heart of modern AI, while Together AI’s commitment to open ecosystems gives enterprises the flexibility to scale on their terms. Equinix Inference Exchange will enable architectures that are neutral by design, open by default and engineered for exceptional performance.” “Equinix Inference Exchange turns the world’s leading digital interconnection platform into a global fabric for AI inference,” said Raj Mirpuri, vice president of global AI clouds and infrastructure ecosystem at NVIDIA. “As accelerated compute becomes a strategic asset class, combining NVIDIA’s infrastructure & technology with Together AI’s open-model inference platform and Equinix’s global reach gives enterprises a powerful, distributed foundation to bring intelligence closer to their data, applications and customers – accelerating the next generation of intelligent services.” “Together AI was built on the conviction that open, accessible AI is what will define the industry moving forward, because enterprises shouldn’t have to choose between model performance and operational flexibility,” said Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO, Together AI. “What we are building with Equinix and NVIDIA proves that model choice and performance are not trade-offs. They are the foundation of enterprise AI done right.” **Where Inference Runs Matters** The pace of enterprise AI adoption is outrunning the infrastructure needed to support it. As enterprise AI moves from experimentation to production, inference increasingly needs to run closer to the users, data and applications it serves across clouds, models, providers and geographies. This shift requires enterprises to determine not only how to deploy AI infrastructure, but where it should run and how it connects to the data, applications and workloads it depends on.
